candidate.title: cP-RNA-Seq
candidate.scope: The cP-RNA-Seq row of the assigned Illumina poster, from Extracted RNA through chemical end selection and adapter-based cDNA library formation. Its three stacked tracks are end-group classes of one treated pool, not separate target methods or independently processed workflows. The adjacent 3Seq/3-Seq/3′-end-seq/PAS-Seq/SS3-Seq/3′T-fill and 3P-Seq rows, the ClickSeq text above, and the click-chemistry panel at right are surrounding context, without a drawn route into this row. The initial highlighted cP icon defines the target and is not a preparative step. The 2016 primary protocol resolves end chemistry and measurement limitations, without adding its unshown enrichment, controls, validation branches or optional adaptations. The final library supports identification of selected RNA sequences; sequencing itself is beyond the final drawn cDNA endpoint.

features: Purple RNA strands are oriented 5′ at left and 3′ at right. The three depicted classes end in 3′-cP (pink), 3′-P (blue), and 3′-OH.

Starting 5′ groups are not specified in the drawing; the paper describes a pool containing either 5′-P or 5′-OH with each of the three 3′ classes.

Introduction, [b00004]
evidence.quote: Any RNAs that fail to ligate with both adapters are not amplified through subsequent RT-PCR reactions, hence they do not appear in the resulting sequencing data.

states.label: Purified amplified cDNA library representing selected RNA inserts
features: The final drawn molecule has a blue cDNA insert between green and orange flanks; the lower blocked RNA tracks have no corresponding final product.
The sequenced carrier is amplified cDNA. Its insert sequence reports RNA identity for molecules that passed end selection and acquired both adapter interfaces.
The initial cP is removed before copying; cP association is supplied by preparation history rather than a retained cP group in the readout.

Selection is not definitive proof of an initial cP: terminal ribose modifications such as 2′-O-methylation can evade periodate and enter the library. The paper also notes reverse-transcription bias from RNA modifications.

operations.label: CIP phosphatase treatment
operations.description: Treat the mixed RNA pool with CIP. Linear terminal phosphates are removed from 5′ and 3′ ends; the 3′-cP class remains protected, while the original 3′-P class becomes 3′-OH.
operations.mechanism: CIP distinguishes a terminal monophosphate from 2′,3′-cyclic phosphate; it does not remove the depicted 3′-cP.
operations.information_effect: Preserves original cP versus non-cP distinction while collapsing original 3′-P and 3′-OH into the same reactive 3′-OH class.

operations.label: Periodate (NaIO4) treatment
operations.description: Modify the exposed 3′-OH termini of the CIP-treated non-cP classes to ligation-incompetent X ends. The cP-bearing class stays intact.
operations.mechanism: Periodate cleaves terminal ribose cis-diols to 2′,3′-dialdehydes; the cyclic phosphate protects that terminal diol interface.
operations.information_effect: Selectivity is encoded as preservation versus loss of the 3′-adapter ligation interface. The blocked RNA molecules remain depicted; ribose-modified RNAs outside the three illustrated classes can also survive.

operations.label: Kinase (T4 PNK) treatment
operations.description: Convert the protected 3′-cP to 3′-OH and add 5′ phosphates. The original cP-derived track becomes compatible with adapter attachment at both ends; the lower tracks retain their 3′-X blocks.
operations.mechanism: The named T4 PNK treatment combines removal of the terminal cyclic phosphate with 5′ phosphorylation, as resolved by the primary paper; its caption alone says Kinase.
operations.information_effect: Makes the chemically selected RNA readable by adapter-based library preparation; the original cP itself is no longer retained.

operations.label: Adaptor ligation
operations.description: Attach the depicted left adapter to all three RNA tracks and the right adapter only to the 3′-OH track derived from original cP RNA. Competitors retain a blocked 3′ end and do not become fully flanked templates.

method_scopes.rationale: All five local blocks belong to the single cP-RNA-Seq target named by the card and middle-row caption.
